siteSource: docs/LUNAR_ADDITIONAL_SITES_RESEARCH.md catalog row 14 (Malapert Crater 1, NPD; distinct from Malapert Massif R23), NASA Lunar Surface Data Book M2M-30044 Table A2.1-1. PGDA/Data Book reference point; center of an original candidate-region polygon; not an approved landing site.

featureNotes.ridge: Highest source pixel within 50 m of the sampled skyline at grid bearing 0 degrees from the near-detail center: the crest of a low swell of the crater floor about 120 m grid-north of it and about 6 m above it, forming the skyline of the initial view. Descriptive label from numeric NPD elevation and illustrative hillshade; not an IAU feature name.
featureNotes.third: Off-grid holdout on the floor grid-west-southwest of the site, about 2.95 km away; no mission significance.
featureNotes.nearDetail: Gentlest 25 m window found within 45 m of the saved point (about 0.15 degree plane-fit slope versus 3.0 degrees at the point), about 24 m grid-west-southwest of it. The surrounding floor slopes under 1 degree within 100 m and 500 m. Selected for scale-figure footing, not landing suitability.
featureNotes.crop: 20 x 20 km, the complete NPD raster, centered on the saved point (which is the raster center). The saved point lies on a nearly flat, cratered floor; the large relief in this product (rises of roughly 230-920 m above the floor) is at the raster's grid-east, grid-southwest and grid-west-northwest edges, so the crop keeps as much of it as the source contains.
featureNotes.view: Initial view faces grid bearing 0 degrees (about 8.4 degrees west of geographic north). A planar raster scan from the near-detail center in 3-degree steps found the skyline to be the floor's low swell 60-250 m away at grid bearings 108-219 and 228-36 degrees, but the raster edge itself at grid bearings 39-105 and 222-225 degrees, where the terrain is still rising when the data stop. Grid bearing 0 keeps both saved views at least 6 degrees away from the raster-edge sectors.
featureNotes.light: Illustrative Blender/QA light from grid bearing about 100 degrees at about 20 degrees elevation, so the view (grid bearing 0) is side-lit. Not an ephemeris Sun; the application lights terrain with its own Sun direction.

siteLimitations: The saved point lies on a nearly flat crater floor. From eye height at the viewpoint, the skyline in most directions is a low swell of that floor 60-250 m away, 2-8 m above the eye; it is not a distant mountain skyline.

Grid-east and grid-northeast (grid bearings about 39-105 degrees from the viewpoint) and grid-southwest (about 222-225 degrees) the terrain rises about 360-920 m toward the NPD raster edges and is still rising where the data stop. Looking in those directions, the modeled skyline is the crop edge, not real terrain; the real skyline is higher. A smaller rise toward the grid-west-northwest edge is also truncated but stays below the near swell as seen from the viewpoint.
Terrain beyond the NPD raster (more than about 10 km from the site) was not checked; higher features outside it can rise above the modeled skyline in every direction.
The astronaut stands on a gently sloping triangle selected for footing; no claim of walkability, safe footing or landing suitability.
